You chose B. So I stayed still, and I listened. And what I heard that morning has been repeated for five thousand years. Stay till the end, because what Krishna showed next, no human eye was meant to see.

Krishna didn't shout. He didn't argue. He smiled, and said softly, Arjuna, why do you grieve? The soul is never born, and it never dies. Weapons cannot cut it. Fire cannot burn it. Water cannot wet it. Wind cannot dry it.
Arjuna wiped his tears. Krishna, he whispered, if it is possible, show me who you really are. Krishna looked at me, then at Arjuna. And the whole battlefield went silent.

Wait, why did the armies freeze? Every soldier stopped. Every arrow hung in the air. And Krishna began to grow. Taller than the chariot. Taller than the trees. A thousand suns blazed behind Him. Thousands of arms. Thousands of faces. The whole universe, inside Him.
Arjuna fell to his knees. And the light was coming straight toward me. So what should I do? Comment A, look straight at Him. Or comment B, shut my eyes and fold my hands. Part three, tomorrow.
